_comment: Text/image-to-video via Wan (Alibaba), using ComfyUI's own NATIVE Wan support
(the WanImageToVideo core node) rather than a third-party wrapper, since core
nodes are far more stable across ComfyUI versions than community wrapper packs.
The starting image is the scene's own already-generated image (see
ComfyUIVideoProvider) - which itself was generated through the IPAdapter
reference-conditioning workflow when a character reference exists. This is
deliberately how character consistency is achieved here: the video model
animates the SAME character-consistent frame rather than re-imagining the
character from text alone, which would be far more likely to drift.
REQUIRES, in your ComfyUI install (on the external high-VRAM machine this is
meant for - this is explicitly NOT for the 2GB reference machine):
1. A Wan 2.1 or 2.2 image-to-video diffusion model in models/diffusion_models/
(e.g. wan2.1_i2v_480p_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors, or a GGUF quant via the
ComfyUI-GGUF custom node pack if VRAM is tighter than the full model needs).
2. The matching Wan VAE in models/vae/ (e.g. wan_2.1_vae.safetensors).
3. The umt5_xxl text encoder in models/text_encoders/ (e.g.
umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors).
4. A CLIP vision model in models/clip_vision/ (clip_vision_h.safetensors -
the same file the IPAdapter workflow uses, if that is already installed).
5. The ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite custom node pack (VHS_VideoCombine), for
muxing the decoded frames into an actual .mp4 - this is one of the most
widely-installed custom node packs and has been stable for a long time,
which is why it was picked over ComfyUI's newer core video-save nodes.
VERSION NOTE, stated plainly: this workflow has not been executed against a
live ComfyUI instance as part of building it - there is no GPU capable of
running Wan available in this development environment. The node graph follows
ComfyUI's documented native Wan I2V example workflow structure, but treat it
the same as any workflow you have not personally run yet: verify it end to end
on your actual deployment hardware, and check the Wan model's exact expected
text-encoder/VAE filenames against whatever version you download.
length is the frame count, not seconds - the caller (ComfyUIVideoProvider)
converts the scene's target duration into a frame count using {{FPS}} before
filling this template. Wan clips are typically generated in the 3-6 second
range per call; a longer scene is generated as one Wan call up to that model's
practical limit rather than attempted in one shot indefinitely.
steps/cfg here are full-quality defaults (not LCM-distilled) - lower steps
trades quality for speed the same way it does for image generation.
